newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco expects 6.0 pct growth by year 2000/2001.
newsitem.headline: Morocco expects 6.0 pct growth by year 2000/2001.

text.p: Morocco expects economic growth of 6.0 percent and inflation of 3.5 percent by the year 2000/2001 compared with zero growth and inflation of 3.0 to 4.0 percent in 1997, Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj said on Tuesday.

Briefing reporters on Morocco's economic indicators, he said: "Based on a medium-term forecast, we expect the Moroccan economy to grow by an annual rate of 6.0 percent of GDP by the year 2000/2001 against zero growth in 1997".
The forecast was based on "a normal agricultural season and resumption of tourism activity," Kabbaj said.
Nearly three million tourists are expected to visit this year, which will generate more than $1 billion, officials said.
Kabbaj said the authorities would try to maintain "the inflation rate at around 3.5 percent on the horizon 2000/2001 against 3.0 to 4.0 percent in 1997".
The current account deficit is expected to remain below 2.0 percent of GDP in the year 2000/2001 compared with 1.5 percent in 1997, Kabbaj said.

The government expects the budget deficit to drop to around 2.7 percent of GDP in 1997/98 against 3.0 percent in 1996/97, the minister said. Morocco's financial year begins on July 1 and ends on June 30.
Under the budget outlined in draft by Kabbaj last month, spending will total around 126.7 billion dirhams compared with 117.1 billion in 1996/97.
Revenue for fiscal 1997/98 was put at 114.3 billion dirhams compared with 107.7 billion in the previous fiscal year.
Morocco, which has total foreign debt of $21 billion, plans to reduce its burden to 45 percent of GDP by the year 2001 against 55 percent of GDP in 1997, Kabbaj said.
The economy, which depends on cyclical changes in the weather, registered 11.8 percent growth last year.
In the 1995/96 season, Morocco harvested 10 million tonnes of cereals against 1.6 million the season before, which was badly affected by drought.
The cereals harvest dropped in 1996/97 to around 3.5 million tonnes, which is expected to pull down GDP growth to stagnation level, he added.
Agriculture represents nearly 20 percent of Morocco's GDP and employs nearly 50 percent of the estimated 10 million workforce.
